### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A04 opened about half of all traces (98 of 200) while A01 was not observed at all; in the later window the picture is reversed — A01 opens about half of the traces (99 of 200, about 0.5 occurrences per trace, never more than once per trace) and A04 is no longer observed. [OCC001, OCC002]
- Both activities appear only as the very first event of a trace (mean position 0 with no spread) — A04 in the earlier window, A01 in the later one — and in both windows roughly half of the traces contain such an entry step while half do not. [POS001, POS002]
- The entry step always leads to A03: in the earlier window every observed outgoing transition of A04 went to A03, and in the later window every observed outgoing transition of A01 goes to A03. [DIR001, DIR002]
- A01 and A04 never occur in the same trace in either window. Before, A04 preceded A03 in about 49 of 100 traces; in the later window A01 precedes A03 in about 50 of 100 traces, with A03 otherwise appearing alone. [REL001, REL002, REL003]
- Separately, routing around A07 and A13 shifted: A07's outgoing transitions moved from about 92% to A13 (remainder A11) to about 56% A13, 29% A03 and 10% A05, and A13 now sends about 32% of its outgoing transitions to A07, which was not observed before (A03 still receives the largest share, about 47%). [DIR003, DIR004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the process entry changed identity: A04, which in the earlier window started about half of the traces and always led directly to A03, is in the later window replaced by A01, which starts about half of the traces and likewise always leads directly to A03. The supporting signs are a near-exact swap in participation (about 49–50 in 100 traces each way), an identical positional profile (first event only), an identical successor (A03 in every observed case), and relational evidence that A01 and A04 are alternatives that never co-occur; eleven control-flow items qualified in screening against roughly 0.14 expected without a change, and every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1000 random re-splits, so sampling fluctuation cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, POS001, POS002, REL001, REL002, REL003]

The evidence cannot distinguish a genuine replacement of A04 by a new activity A01 from a renaming of the same step, and zero participation formally means only that A04 was not observed in the later sample. [OCC001, OCC002]

Other differences: the redistribution between A07, A13, A03 and A05 — including the previously unobserved transitions A13→A07 and A07→A03 — is not part of the entry-change hypothesis and may reflect a separate routing change; its exact shares rest on only 48–59 outgoing transitions per window, so the proportions are uncertain. [DIR003, DIR004]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 28 units tested, 11 items qualified, 0.14 expected without change. All in control_flow family. 11 items vs 0.14 expected — that's many times larger (about 79x). So the count cannot be explained by chance. This means we go beyond "insufficient evidence" based on screening counts.

Now the evidence items:

- OCC001: A01 went from 0 participation (0 occurrences in 200 traces) to ~0.495 participation (99 of 200 traces, mean 0.495 per trace). So A01 appeared in about half the traces in the later window, absent before.
- OCC002: A04 went from 0.49 participation (98 of 200) to 0. So A04 disappeared in the later window.
- DIR001: A01's outgoing transitions: before empty (A01 never occurred), after 100% to A03. So when A01 occurs, it's always followed by A03.
- DIR002: A04's outgoing transitions: before 100% to A03, after empty (A04 never occurs).
- DIR003: A07's outgoing: before mostly A13 (0.917) and A11 (0.083); after A03 0.288, A13 0.559, A05 0.102, A11 0.051. So A07 now sometimes goes to A03 (~29% of A07's outgoing transitions) and A05 (~10%), while A13 share dropped from ~92% to ~56%.
- DIR004: A13's outgoing: before A03 0.77, A11 0.17, A05 0.06; after A07 0.32, A03 0.47, A05 0.07, A11 0.14. So A13 now sometimes goes to A07 (~32%).
- POS001: A01 position support 0 → 0.495, mean position 0 in both (when present). Position mean 0 — A01 occurs at the very start of traces (position 0). Actually mean 0, std 0, so A01 always at position 0? That's interesting — A01 is the first event.
- POS002: A04 position support 0.49 → 0, mean 0. So A04 also occurred at position 0 before.

So the picture: A04 occurred at the start of about half the traces before, always followed by A03. In the later window, A04 is gone, and A01 appears at the start of about half the traces, always followed by A03. This looks like A04 was replaced by A01 at the start of traces — a substitution/replacement of one start activity by another.

REL001 (A01, A03): before, A03 only (B_only = 1.0); after, cooccurrence 0.495 with A_before_B 0.495, B_only 0.505. So A01 and A03 now occur together in half the traces, always A01 before A03.
REL002 (A01, A04): before, A04 only 0.49, neither 0.51; after, A01 only 0.495, neither 0.505. They never co-occur — they're alternatives occupying the same slot.
REL003 (A03, A04): before, cooccurrence 0.49 with B_before_A (A04 before A03) 0.49, A03_only 0.51; after, A03_only 1.0. So A04 always preceded A03 before; now A04 is gone.

So the main hypothesis: the initial activity A04 (which occurred in about half the traces, always followed by A03) was replaced by A01, which now occurs in about half the traces, always at the start and always followed by A03. This is a replacement of one path/activity by another — not a shift in path frequencies.

Additionally, DIR003 and DIR004 show redistribution: A07 now sometimes leads to A03 (~29% of its outgoing transitions vs 0 before), and A13 now sometimes leads to A07 (~32% vs 0 before). Hmm, wait — A13 → A07? Before, A13's outgoing were A03 (77%), A11 (17%), A05 (6%). After: A07 (32%), A03 (47%), A05 (7%), A11 (14%). And A07's outgoing before: A13 (92%), A11 (8%); after: A03 (29%), A13 (56%), A05 (10%), A11 (5%).

So there's a new cycle A13 → A07 → A13? Or A13 → A07 → A03. Interesting. These are secondary differences — new routing between A07, A13, A03, A05.

Wait, but are DIR003/DIR004 part of the main hypothesis or separate? The main hypothesis is the A04→A01 replacement at the start. The A07/A13 changes are additional routing changes. Let me think about whether they could be connected. A04 → A03 always. A01 → A03 always. The A07/A13 redistribution involves A03 gaining share from A13 in A07's outgoing, and A07 appearing in A13's outgoing. These seem like separate behavioural differences — perhaps a new loop or path involving A07 and A13. I'll report them under "Other differences".

Actually, let me reconsider: could the A07/A13 changes be part of the same underlying change? The replacement of A04 by A01 wouldn't naturally cause A13 to start going to A07. These are distinct. I'll report them separately.

Support level: The screening count is 11 items vs 0.14 expected — many times larger, so chance can't explain the whole set. The hypothesis (A04 replaced by A01 as the starting activity before A03) is directly supported by multiple consistent items: OCC001, OCC002 (participation swap), DIR001, DIR002 (both always followed by A03), POS001, POS002 (both at position 0), REL001, REL002, REL003 (relational evidence: A01 and A04 never co-occur, each alternates with A03, A04 preceded A03 before, A01 precedes A03 now).

This is direct, consistent relational + positional + participation evidence. Competing explanations: could it be that A01 and A04 are the same activity renamed? We can't rule out that the activity was relabelled — but from the evidence's perspective, the behaviour is that one start activity disappeared and another appeared in its place. Another competing explanation: sampling — but with 200 traces each and ~49% participation vs 0%, that's not sampling fluctuation; empirical strength 0.995 for each. Also, could A01 have existed before but not been observed? Zero participation only means not observed — but with 200 traces and it appearing in 99 after, absence in 200 before is strong. Still, a limitation: we observe replacement, not why; and we cannot tell whether A01 is a renamed A04 (the evidence cannot distinguish a relabelling from a genuine substitution). Hmm, but the instructions say don't speculate about causes. The competing explanation to mention: the evidence shows the two activities occupy the same slot but cannot show whether A01 is a renamed version of A04 or a genuinely different activity taking over that role. Actually that's more of an interpretation limit. Another competing explanation: rare variant — A01 could be a rare variant that happened to appear... no, 99/200 is not rare.

Is this "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The evidence directly shows: A04 present in ~half of before traces at position 0, always → A03; absent after. A01 absent before, present in ~half of after traces at position 0, always → A03. REL002 shows they never co-occur (alternatives in the same slot). This is direct, consistent, multi-indicator evidence for a substitution: the pre-trace activity A04 was replaced by A01. I'd say Supported hypothesis. The relational evidence (REL) directly shows the change in how the activities relate. The hypothesis "A04 was replaced by A01 as the initial step before A03" is directly shown.

Limitations: we cannot determine whether A01 is a renamed A04 or a different activity; and the secondary A07/A13 routing changes are not explained by this hypothesis.

Now, per instructions: "If the evidence also shows other differences that are not part of this hypothesis, report them afterwards under 'Other differences:' without adding their activities to the main hypothesis."

So main hypothesis: replacement of the initial activity A04 by A01, both executing directly before A03 at the start of about half the traces.

Other differences: routing redistribution around A07 and A13 — A13 now leads to A07 in about a third of its outgoing transitions (was never observed before), and A07 now leads to A03 in about 29% of its outgoing transitions (was never observed before), with A13's share from A07 dropping from ~92% to ~56%. This suggests a new connection between A13 and A07, but it's a secondary observation.

Wait — should the A07/A13 changes be part of the main hypothesis? The main hypothesis is about the A04/A01 substitution. The A07/A13 redistribution is a separate structural change (new edges A13→A07 and A07→A03). I'll keep them separate.

Hmm, actually, let me reconsider whether the whole thing could be one coherent change: maybe the process restructured such that A04's role is now played by A01, and separately a loop A13↔A07 was added. The evidence doesn't tie them together. Keep separate.

Support level decision: The screening comparison: 11 items vs 0.14 expected — count many times larger, so chance as a whole can't explain it. Then judge by directness, consistency, ruling out competitors. The A04→A01 replacement hypothesis: direct participation evidence (OCC), direct directional evidence (DIR001/DIR002: both always followed by A03), direct positional evidence (POS: both at position 0 when present), direct relational evidence (REL001-003). Very consistent. Competing explanation: relabelling — the evidence cannot distinguish "A04 renamed to A01" from "A04 removed and A01 introduced". Either way, the behavioural description is the same: the start activity changed identity. I think "Supported hypothesis" is right. The evidence directly and consistently shows the substitution.

Actually, let me double check the "hypothesis about order or placement needs relational or positional evidence" — we have both REL and POS. Good.

One more check on the "change in how often existing paths are taken" condition — not applicable here since A01 was absent before and A04 absent after; this is a replacement, which I should not frame as a path-frequency shift. Correct.

Numbers to use:
- A01: 0 of 200 traces before → 99 of 200 (~50 in 100) after; mean ~0.5 occurrences per trace (so never repeated — recurrence_support 0, mean = participation, so exactly once when present).
- A04: 98 of 200 (~49 in 100) before → 0 after.
- Both always at the first position of the trace (mean position 0, std 0).
- Both always followed by A03 (100% of outgoing transitions).
- REL002: A01 and A04 never occur in the same trace in either window (cooccurrence 0).
- REL003: before, A04 preceded A03 in 49 of 100 traces (cooccurrence 0.49, B_before_A 0.49); after, A03 occurs in all traces without A04.
- REL001: after, A01 before A03 in ~50 of 100 traces; before, A03 always without A01.

Secondary: DIR003: A07's outgoing transitions: before ~92% to A13, ~8% to A11 (48 outgoing observations); after ~56% to A13, ~29% to A03, ~10% to A05, ~5% to A11 (59 observations). DIR004: A13's outgoing: before ~77% to A03, ~17% to A11, ~6% to A05; after ~47% to A03, ~32% to A07, ~7% to A05, ~14% to A11.

Note DIR shares are over outgoing transitions of the source, not cases — I should phrase accordingly.

Also note: A01 and A04 each occur at most once per trace (mean occurrences = participation, recurrence support 0).

Empirical strength 0.995 for all items — each difference is larger than ~995 of 1000 random re-splits. I can mention this briefly but the main weight is on the screening count and directness.
